generatedProse.concept-context: Research across the School of Sport often collects sensitive personal data, so the duties of confidentiality, consent and anonymity carry real weight. A coaching study records young athletes, a sport therapy project holds injury and medical histories, a management survey captures members' health and income. Participants take part on the understanding that their responses are secure and that they cannot be identified in any write-up. Where a study involves children or vulnerable groups, which coaching and physical education work often does, these duties tighten, and the research ethics committee expects to see the extra safeguards.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching students finish the same set of filmed sessions and interviews with a youth football squad and turn to writing up.

Tom labels the video clips with the players' names, shares the raw footage with his coaching mentor without asking, and keeps the files on a personal phone. The write-up reads vividly, but consent for sharing was never secured, and named clips make the children identifiable. The duties of confidentiality, consent and anonymity have all been missed.

Amara secures signed consent from parents and assent from the players before filming, stores the footage securely, and reports the squad as Player 1 and Player 2. Because the participants are under eighteen, she checks the extra safeguarding requirements with the research ethics committee first. The data still tells its story, but no child can be identified from it.

Both students gathered the same material. Only Amara treated the young players behind the data as owed confidentiality, consent and anonymity.
generatedProse.summary: Collecting data in the School of Sport brings duties to the people who provide it, from athletes to club members to rehabilitation patients. You can now apply the duties of confidentiality, consent and anonymity, justify the extra care that children and vulnerable participants require, and appraise how sport data should be secured, shared and anonymised. The final lesson widens the view to rigour across the whole project.

check.body: A sport coaching study films training sessions with a youth squad. Why does involving children call for additional care?

items.text: Because they may be less able to give fully informed, voluntary consent, so extra safeguards and expert advice are needed.
Because footage of children is more interesting to examiners.
Because anonymisation is not required for children.
Because consent forms do not apply to anyone under eighteen.

feedback.correct: That's right. Reduced capacity to give informed, voluntary consent means extra safeguards and advice are needed.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about capacity to consent, not convenience.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Children and vulnerable participants may be less able to consent fully, so the duties tighten and expert advice is needed; they do not relax.
